TEXT
Freedom of speech is one of the most precious rights in a democratic society. It allows people to express their opinions, criticise their leaders and defend their rights without fear. Thanks to this freedom, injustices can be exposed, and societies can progress. A country where people cannot speak freely is a country where corruption and oppression can grow in the dark. However, freedom of speech also comes with responsibilities. It does not give anyone the right to insult others, to spread lies or to encourage hatred and violence. True freedom of expression respects the dignity of others and serves the truth. As one thinker said, "Your freedom ends where the freedom of others begins." Learning to use this right wisely is the sign of a mature and civilised society.

I. READING COMPREHENSION (8 marks)
1) Why is freedom of speech so precious in a democracy?   (2 marks)
2) What can happen in a country where people cannot speak freely?   (2 marks)
3) What does freedom of speech NOT give the right to do?   (2 marks)
4) Explain the quotation: "Your freedom ends where the freedom of others begins."   (2 marks)

II. LANGUAGE (6 marks)
1) Complete with a relative pronoun (who / where): A country ______ people cannot speak freely is dangerous.   (1,5 marks)
2) Put into the passive: "This freedom allows people to express their opinions."   (2 marks)
3) Give the opposite of "freedom" = ______.   (1,5 marks)
4) Complete with a linker (however / because): Freedom of speech is precious; ______, it comes with responsibilities.   (1 mark)

III. WRITING (6 marks)
"Should freedom of speech have limits?" Write a composition (about 12-14 lines) giving your opinion, with arguments and examples. Use linkers.
